# pai tests

Test governance: audit a repo's tests, prune them to the governed core

```
pai tests <command>
```

Tests stay only with evidence (tests/KEPT.md): (a) a real fix they guarded, (b) a security or destructive-operation guard, (c) an external contract. UI/simulator targets, snapshot baselines and run outputs (.xcresult, recordings, screenshots, DerivedData) are classified too; outputs are always dropped unless listed. `audit` reads git and files only and never runs a test. `prune` prints the plan; with --apply a worker (orchestrate class) removes the rest on its own branch and commits; you land it. The growth alarm (config tests.growthAlarm, default 20) tells the session when a project's suite outgrows its core or a gate run reports more than 500 tests.

```sh
pai tests audit --repo .
pai tests prune --repo ~/code/app
pai tests prune --repo ~/code/app --apply
```

See also: `pai worker merge`

### pai tests audit

List test files with a proposed class and the file-count trend

```
pai tests audit [options]
```

Per file: KEEP-a/b/c with evidence, or DROP; then test files per month and a proposed tests/KEPT.md. Read-only.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--repo PATH` | string | — | Repository (default: the current directory) |
| `--all` | flag | — | List every file (default: the first 60) |
| `--json` | flag | — | Machine-readable JSON |

```sh
pai tests audit
pai tests audit --repo ~/code/app --all
```

### pai tests prune

Plan, or with --apply start a worker, that prunes the suite to the governed core

```
pai tests prune [options]
```

Without --apply prints the plan. With --apply starts `pai worker run --class orchestrate` in the repo: git rm the DROP files and test-only fixtures, write tests/KEPT.md, keep the test script and build working, one commit. It never merges.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--repo PATH` | string | — | Repository (default: the current directory) |
| `--apply` | flag | — | Start the worker (default: print the plan) |

```sh
pai tests prune
pai tests prune --repo ~/code/app --apply
```

## Subcommands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `pai tests audit` | List test files with a proposed class and the file-count trend |
